text:
mike_infra: Heads up — ap-southeast1 is seeing a sustained IOPS spike (~12k-18k) and a corresponding bump in GPU attach latency starting ~02:10 UTC. Correlates with a bunch of ephemeral cleaner dirty-page flushes.

sara_sre: Link to grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pgxNVMe/ephemeral-io?orgId=1 (look at write_iops and reclaim rate) :eyes:

devon_eng: Confirmed. `writeback_reclaim` kernel counter jumps at same times. KV-cache expansion + overlayfs fsyncs seem to line up.

janet_ops: Any recent janitor/cleaner rollout? I saw a canary yesterday to tighten eviction aggressiveness.

mike_infra: Yes — cleaner v2.8 rolled to 20% last night. My suspicion: more aggressive dirty-page aggregation -> big synchronous flushes under certain tempfile patterns.

infra-bot: ALERT: nvme_io_ops > 15000 in ap-southeast1 (detected 1729009952). Affected hosts: gnode-aps1-[0123].

devon_eng: Snippet from dmesg on gnode-aps1-02: ```
[ 1023.456789] writeback: start io 0x7f9a34
[ 1023.457001] nvme0n1: submission queue stalled
[ 1023.457120] fsync: waiting for dirty pages to flush (user pid 2431)
```

sara_sre: We should avoid mass flushes during GPU attach windows. Current attach window is 02:00-03:30 UTC for APAC bursters.

janet_ops: Short-term mitigations: 1) Pause rollout of cleaner v2.8 2) Add QoS cap on janitor IO during attach window 3) Mark node pool as drainable for noncritical batch jobs. Thoughts?

mike_infra: +1 to pausing rollout. QoS cap is doable quickly (ioq cgroup tweak). Marking pool drainable is a manual ops step — I'll trigger.

devon_eng: We can also experiment with splitting dirty_ratio tuning on a small canary to reduce synchronous flush sizes: `echo 5 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio` on canary nodes. But that increases latency on single writes. Tradeoff note.

sara_sre: Cost/availability tradeoffs: throttling janitor will increase janitor backlog and delay reclaimed space, potentially increasing SSD wear later. But immediate impact on GPU attach is primary SLA concern.

mike_infra: Action items:
- mike_infra: pause v2.8 rollout (done 1729009988)
- mike_infra: apply io cgroup cap to janitor on gnode-aps1 pool (planned 1729010200)
- devon_eng: spin canary with dirty_ratio=5 and monitor (ETA 30m)
- sara_sre: open internal incident ticket and update apac oncall (INC-2024-287)

janet_ops: I'll coordinate pool draining and bump up monitoring alerts to a lower threshold while we observe.

devon_eng: After pausing rollout, I still want to root-cause the workload pattern that triggers huge fsync batches. I'll pull sample traces from node-level perf and janitor logs.

sara_sre: If we see persistent / worst-case spikes, fallback option is to route GPU attach requests to eu nodes for the next 1-2 hours while we stabilize. That costs cross-region egress but keeps SLAs.

mike_infra: Agreed. For now: pausing rollout + IO cap + canary. I'll post updates. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: NOTE: cleaner-v2.8 rollout paused at 1729009988 by mike_infra.

mike_infra: Update @everyone — applied ioq cap and started canary. Early telemetry after 10m: write_iops on canary down ~45%, attach latency improved by ~120ms median.

sara_sre: Nice. Keep monitoring for wear/regression delta. If good after 1h we can roll a more conservative configuration instead of reverting permanently.

janet_ops: Ticket INC-2024-287 updated with mitigation steps and owners. Closing thread for now; will reopen if metrics worsen. :white_check_mark:
